messages.content:
You are checking a research plan against a list of experimental controls. You are not asked whether the plan is good. For each control of the list you give two separate answers: CONTENT (does the plan state this control?) and PLACE (is the passage written under an experiment that it can check?).

PLAN. A sequence of actions written one after the other by a planner. Each action adds or revises one proposed experiment and usually has the fields ACTION, TITLE, PROPOSAL, CONTROLS, COST and PREDICTION. Actions are separated by blank lines and are given in the order they were written. Every action counts, including an action that revises an earlier one and an action that looks incomplete.

REFERENCE CONTROLS. A list of experimental controls. Each has an identifier and a description.

CONTENT. Give exactly one content status for each reference control. Judge the content only, wherever the passage is written in the plan.
- "conforme": a passage of the plan states what the description requires (what is compared, held fixed, varied, repeated, measured or excluded). Different wording is fine. Nothing essential is missing or weakened.
- "altere": a passage of the plan states a recognisable but partial, vaguer, reduced or modified version of the control.
- "absent": no passage of the plan states this control.
If the control is stated in several places, keep the best content status found (conforme, then altere, then absent) and quote the passage that earns it. If several passages earn the same best status, quote one whose PLACE is "checks" if there is one.

PLACE. Only for "conforme" and "altere". Read the action that contains your quote, and judge it against the experiment that this action proposes (its TITLE and PROPOSAL), not against the description of the reference control. If that action has no TITLE and no PROPOSAL, answer "general" if the quoted control is general, otherwise "cannot_check".
- "checks": this experiment is one whose result the quoted control would check.
- "cannot_check": this experiment has nothing for the quoted control to compare, hold fixed, vary, repeat, measure or exclude.
- "general": the quoted control names no model, dataset, metric, quantity, condition or comparison that belongs to one experiment; it would apply to any experiment of the plan.
For "absent", PLACE is null. Your PLACE answer must never change your CONTENT answer.

Rules.
1. Judge each reference control on its own. One passage may support several controls.
2. Judge only what is written. Do not credit a control because it would be sensible, usual or implied. Do not lower a status for style, length, order or cost.
3. Evidence. For "conforme" and "altere", quote the passage that carries the control. Copy it character for character from a single action: no ellipsis, no added or removed word, no corrected spelling, no changed punctuation, no paraphrase. Take the shortest passage that is enough: at least 24 characters, at most 300 characters; if the whole field that carries the control is shorter than 24 characters, quote the whole field. A program searches the plan for your quote, word for word; a quote that is not found counts as "absent".
4. For "absent", the quote is null.
5. Give an answer for every reference control, and for no other identifier.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form:
{"<identifier>": {"content": "conforme" | "altere" | "absent", "quote": "<quote>" | null, "place": "checks" | "cannot_check" | "general" | null}, ...}

PLAN
<<<
ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of shuffling the few-shot examples on median latency per query for Ilexa-6
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ilexa-6 on the Pryce reasoning chains and measure median latency per query before and after shuffling the few-shot examples. All runs share one data order for the Pryce reasoning chains, so that differences in median latency per query cannot come from batching. Each configuration of Ilexa-6 is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints.
CONTROLS: (1) Run Ilexa-6 on the Pryce reasoning chains with five random seeds and report the spread of median latency per query. (2) Include Dromond-8 as a baseline under the same training budget. (3) Match the number of training steps between Ilexa-6 and Dromond-8, with seeds {11, 23, 47}.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Median latency per query improves by a small but reliable margin on the Pryce reasoning chains.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of replacing the system prompt with a neutral one on agreement with the reference labels for Pelleas-4
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Pelleas-4 on the Wexcombe caption set and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after replacing the system prompt with a neutral one. The analysis is restricted to the examples of the Wexcombe caption set that Pelleas-4 answers correctly before the intervention. A secondary readout is mean token overlap, reported on the held-out split of the Wexcombe caption set.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Pelleas-4 and Corvane-12. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Wexcombe caption set as a negative control for agreement with the reference labels. (3) Include Corvane-12 as a baseline under the same training budget.
COST: 33 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in agreement with the reference labels beyond seed noise on the Wexcombe caption set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of distilling into a 4-bit student on false-alarm rate at fixed recall for Sundrow-M
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Sundrow-M on the Avenel retrieval pool and measure false-alarm rate at fixed recall before and after distilling into a 4-bit student. If false-alarm rate at fixed recall moves while rank correlation with the gold ordering stays flat, we attribute the change to distilling into a 4-bit student rather than to capacity.
CONTROLS: (1) Run Sundrow-M on the Avenel retrieval pool with five random seeds and report the spread of false-alarm rate at fixed recall. (2) Run Sundrow-M on the Avenel retrieval pool with five random seeds and report the spread of false-alarm rate at fixed recall. (3) Include Brindle-XL as a baseline under the same training budget.
COST: 9 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in false-alarm rate at fixed recall beyond seed noise on the Avenel retrieval pool.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of swapping the tokenizer vocabulary on edit distance to the reference for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Osric code suite and measure edit distance to the reference before and after swapping the tokenizer vocabulary. A secondary readout is exact-match accuracy, reported on the held-out split of the Osric code suite. We plan one pilot run on a tenth of the Osric code suite to check that edit distance to the reference is not saturated before the full experiment.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate swapping the tokenizer vocabulary alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on edit distance to the reference. (2) Include Ostrava-7 as a baseline under the same training budget. (3) Match the number of training steps between Quillon-L and Ostrava-7.
COST: 23 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Edit distance to the reference improves by a small but reliable margin on the Osric code suite.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of halving the learning rate on calibration error for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Brenna-QA set and measure calibration error before and after halving the learning rate. All runs share one data order for the Brenna-QA set, so that differences in calibration error cannot come from batching. A secondary readout is refusal rate, reported on the held-out split of the Brenna-QA set. Each configuration of Varnok-2B is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate halving the learning rate alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on calibration error. (2) Shuffle the labels of the Brenna-QA set as a negative control for calibration error. (3) Evaluate on the Kettering proofs as a held-out distribution.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in calibration error beyond seed noise on the Brenna-QA set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of shuffling the few-shot examples on median latency per query for Ilexa-6
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Ilexa-6 on the Pryce reasoning chains and measure median latency per query before and after shuffling the few-shot examples. We also evaluate transfer to the Tolwyn dialogue logs without further tuning of Ilexa-6. All runs share one data order for the Pryce reasoning chains, so that differences in median latency per query cannot come from batching.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate shuffling the few-shot examples alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on median latency per query. (2) Repeat the evaluation of median latency per query on the Pryce reasoning chains with a second prompt template. (3) Match the number of training steps between Ilexa-6 and Dromond-8.
COST: 28 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Median latency per query degrades on the Tolwyn dialogue logs while it holds on the Pryce reasoning chains.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of replacing the system prompt with a neutral one on agreement with the reference labels for Pelleas-4
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Pelleas-4 on the Wexcombe caption set and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after replacing the system prompt with a neutral one. Each configuration of Pelleas-4 is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints.
CONTROLS: (1) Include Corvane-12 as a baseline under the same training budget. (2) Repeat the evaluation of agreement with the reference labels on the Wexcombe caption set with a second prompt template. (3) Ablate replacing the system prompt with a neutral one alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on agreement with the reference labels.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in agreement with the reference labels beyond seed noise on the Wexcombe caption set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of distilling into a 4-bit student on false-alarm rate at fixed recall for Sundrow-M
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Sundrow-M on the Avenel retrieval pool and measure false-alarm rate at fixed recall before and after distilling into a 4-bit student. A null result on false-alarm rate at fixed recall would still be informative if rank correlation with the gold ordering on the Halvard corpus also stays within its usual range.
CONTROLS: (1) Repeat the evaluation of false-alarm rate at fixed recall on the Avenel retrieval pool with a second prompt template. (2) Ablate distilling into a 4-bit student alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on false-alarm rate at fixed recall. (3) Evaluate on the Halvard corpus as a held-out distribution.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: False-alarm rate at fixed recall improves by a small but reliable margin on the Avenel retrieval pool.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of swapping the tokenizer vocabulary on edit distance to the reference for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Osric code suite and measure edit distance to the reference before and after swapping the tokenizer vocabulary. If edit distance to the reference moves while exact-match accuracy stays flat, we attribute the change to swapping the tokenizer vocabulary rather than to capacity. We expect the effect of swapping the tokenizer vocabulary to be smaller for Ostrava-7 than for Quillon-L, because Ostrava-7 was never exposed to the Marisol summaries.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Quillon-L and Ostrava-7. (2) Repeat the evaluation of edit distance to the reference on the Osric code suite with a second prompt template. (3) Evaluate on the Marisol summaries as a held-out distribution.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Edit distance to the reference degrades on the Marisol summaries while it holds on the Osric code suite.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of halving the learning rate on calibration error for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Brenna-QA set and measure calibration error before and after halving the learning rate. The hypothesis is that halving the learning rate changes calibration error on the Brenna-QA set by more than run-to-run noise. Each configuration of Varnok-2B is trained for the same number of steps and evaluated at three checkpoints. We compare against Tessel-9, trained with the same budget on the Brenna-QA set.
CONTROLS: (1) Report refusal rate on the Brenna-QA set to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric. (2) Repeat the evaluation of calibration error on the Brenna-QA set with a second prompt template. (3) Include Tessel-9 as a baseline under the same training budget.
COST: 37 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Calibration error improves by a small but reliable margin on the Brenna-QA set.
>>>

REFERENCE CONTROLS
- id: c1 | description: Compare against Corvane-12 as a baseline trained with an identical budget.
- id: c2 | description: Repeat the run of Sundrow-M on the Avenel retrieval pool over several random seeds and report the variation of false-alarm rate at fixed recall.
- id: c3 | description: Isolate the effect of truncating the context to 2,000 tokens on recall at 5 by changing it alone, with data and optimizer held fixed.
- id: c4 | description: Hold the number of training steps equal between Marrow-3 and Halden-S.
